reader.requirement: At --std 85 the compiler must refuse a NEXT GROUP clause, in any of its three forms (integer-1, PLUS integer-2, NEXT PAGE), written in a REPORT FOOTING (RF) or PAGE HEADING (PH) report group, under either spelling of the TYPE, and must accept it in RH, CH, DE, CF and PF groups.

edition-consulted.switches: Edition.DialectLevel < 2002 adds the 1985-only SR1 check (a NEXT GROUP needs a LINE NUMBER clause in the group) and, via ExceedsThreeSignificantDigits85, SR2's three-digit limit; the PH/RF refusal that implements SR5 is not gated, so it is the same code at every edition

reader.edition-search: grep DialectLevel in ReportSectionBinder.cs: the only edition tests in BindNextGroupClauses are line 915 (SR1) and line 940 (SR2); the PH/RF branch at line 920 is unconditional
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for SR5 itself; 1985 adds SR1 and SR2 on the same clause, which a later edition does not have)
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness covers PH with the relative form only, spelled TYPE PH; RF, the absolute and NEXT PAGE forms, the spelled-out TYPE words, and the accept half in the other five group types are not exercised

reader.notes: The PH/RF refusal is unconditional and fires for every NEXT GROUP form and either TYPE spelling at --std 85, and the other five group types accept the clause. The diagnostic text cites §2023:13.18.37.3 SR4 instead of the 1985 rule, which names the same prohibition, so the citation is cosmetic, not a wrong verdict.
